$schema-note: The single source of truth for what CI runs and when. `select.py` reads it to decide which suites a change needs; the workflows run nothing that is not in here; `test_selection.py` checks it against the repository. Editing a workflow's job list is not a way to change what runs — edit this file.
unclaimed_policy_note: A changed path that no suite claims and that `ignored` does not list makes the selection every suite, never none. A new component must not be able to merge untested because nobody added a routing rule for it, and `test_selection.py` fails on an unclaimed top-level path so that the fallback stays a safety net rather than the normal case.
ignored_note: Prose and stubs. `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/` are read by people and agents and by no test, so a change to one of them selects nothing but the routing check; `examples/`, `tools/` and `ui/` hold stub READMEs only and get a routing rule on the day they hold code — which `test_selection.py` will demand, because a directory cannot be both ignored and the home of a suite's component. The component READMEs are listed one by one rather than as a `*/README.md` pattern, because the directories they sit in are otherwise routed and an inherited wildcard would be a second kind of rule to reason about.

routing.what: This file against the repository: the consumers of contracts/ and tests/harness/ derived from the dependency graph, every Rust test target claimed, every top-level path routed.
routing.triggers_note: `*` means every change, including one that only touches prose: this suite is cheap, has no dependencies, and is the thing that proves the rest of the table is honest. `.github/` is named as well so that a change to this table selects *this* suite and not the whole matrix — safe only because the checks in `test_selection.py` derive the consumer sets from the repository, so a rule narrowed by mistake fails here rather than passing quietly.

harness.what: The shared harness's own unit tests — the stub LLM, the poller, the deterministic id — with no Docker and no stack.

clerk.what: The clerk at its process boundary, against the shared test stack for the bus and a real Buzz relay the suite brings up itself: one post per suggestion across a redelivery and a restart, nothing of a contact on the relay, the journal with its reach, the activity feed and what it leaves out, and the sweep that deletes an expired suggestion's post.
clerk.run: cargo test --lib --test activite --test approbations --test journal --test smoke --test sweep

sdk-python.what: The Python persona SDK's pure half: the consent gate, the deterministic ids, the envelopes, the completion reader, the language list — stdlib only, against the contract's own fixtures.

sensor.what: The Sensor at its process boundary, against the shared test stack: normalisation, consent, the owner, the owner's own device, bridge bots, presence, encryption, persistence, observability.
sensor.run: cargo test --lib --test bridge_bots_are_not_contacts --test consent --test encryption --test excerpt_consent --test fidelity --test message_to_event --test observability --test outbound --test outbound_message_sent --test owner_device --test owner_is_never_a_contact --test persistence --test presence --test presence_network --test reactions --test sensor_lifecycle --test smoke
sensor.triggers_note: The Gateway's OpenAPI description is in here because the Sensor's one HTTP seam reads `GET /api/consent/snapshot` from it and `sensor/tests/harness/gateway.rs` is a stub that transcribes that endpoint's shape. `test_selection.py` derives that dependency from the repository, so removing this line fails the routing check rather than going unnoticed.

sensor-deployment.what: The reference deployment, twice from the Sensor's side: the whole stack with the four bridges up, and the same stack with no bridge variable set at all.

gateway.what: The Companion Gateway at its process boundary: the session, the consent journal and its snapshot, bootstrap, the bridge facade and its status webhook, approvals, suggestions, settings, the portal register, and the OpenAPI description against the routes it serves.
gateway.run: cargo test --lib --test approvals --test bootstrap --test bridge_status --test bridges --test consent --test consent_snapshot --test hermes_answers --test openapi --test pending --test portals --test service --test settings --test signin --test suggestions

gateway-deployment.what: The Gateway inside the reference deployment, and the portal register against real portal rooms built after it was already running.

hermes.what: The Hermes runtime and the reference persona at their process boundaries: the persona container against the bus and the stub LLM, the runtime starting it, activation, the suggestion policy, the reasoning budget, the language fallback, and the settings the runtime reads from the Gateway.
hermes.run: cargo test --lib --test assistant --test hermes_seam --test language_fallback --test reasoning_budget --test runtime_lifecycle --test runtime_settings --test smoke --test suggestion

hermes-full-loop.what: The whole loop on the reference deployment: a message in a Matrix room, the Sensor, the deployment's own Hermes, a suggestion, an approval through the Gateway, and the reply posted back into the room.

companion.what: The Companion's own checks: the generated Gateway client against companion-gateway/openapi.yaml, svelte-check, the Vitest units, the static export, and the Playwright projects that need no stack.

companion-e2e-stack.what: The Companion's journeys against a real Companion Gateway and a real Synapse behind /api: bootstrap and the in-browser cryptographic setup, the network logins, the dashboard, approvals, consent with a real Sensor, the conversation chooser, and the session that expires and comes back.
companion-e2e-stack.run: npm ci && npx playwright install chromium && npm run build && npm run test:e2e:stack

shared_paths.contracts/: The versioned CloudEvents contract. Read by the harness's validator, by the Sensor, by the Python SDK's tests, and quoted by the Companion's generated client.
shared_paths.tests/harness/: The shared integration-test harness: a dev dependency of sensor/, hermes/, companion-gateway/ and clerk/, and the compose stack the Companion's real-stack e2e brings up.
shared_paths.companion-gateway/openapi.yaml: The Gateway's own HTTP description, and the source the Companion's API client is generated from.

shared_paths_note: These are the paths whose consumers `test_selection.py` derives from the repository rather than taking this file's word for. A change to one of them must run the consumers' suites — that rule is what the two red-`main` incidents cost, and the test is what keeps it true when a fourth consumer appears.
